title: A finite set in a scheme with an ample invertible sheaf lies in an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every finite set $E\subseteq X$ there exists an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ample-proj-open] choose an open immersion j : X → Proj(S) [def-pc-proj]. Let W = j.coborderRange, the complement of closure(image(j)) minus image(j). Mathlib Scheme.Hom.liftCoborder factors j through a closed immersion into W, and subset_coborder puts j(E) inside W.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, first paragraph: Proposition 01Q3 gives an open subscheme of Proj

proof.text: Let s be the set of all positive-degree homogeneous f for which D_+(f) is contained in W, and let I be the homogeneous ideal generated by s. Ideal.homogeneous_span proves homogeneity, and HomogeneousIdeal.mem_irrelevant_of_mem gives I ⊆ S_+. By the basis clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], every point x of j(E) lies in some D_+(f) with f in s. Thus I is contained in none of the point primes of j(E). No finite selection of generators is necessary.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, second paragraph: standard opens form a basis and E is finite

proof.text: Enumerate the finite set j(E) by Fin(card(j(E))). Apply [lem-sc-graded-prime-avoidance] to I and these point primes to obtain a positive-degree homogeneous f in I avoiding every point prime, hence j(E) ⊆ D_+(f). If x is outside W, every generator g in s belongs to its prime, since D_+(g) ⊆ W. Ideal.span_le then puts I inside that prime, so f also belongs to it. Therefore D_+(f) ⊆ W. This works also when E is empty.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, third paragraph: apply Algebra Lemma 00JS to I and the point primes

proof.text: By [def-pc-proj], Mathlib Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen makes V = D_+(f) affine. Since V ⊆ W, IsAffineOpen.preimage_of_isOpenImmersion gives an affine open in W. Pull it back through the closed immersion j.liftCoborder [def-weil-closed-immersion]; this is affine because closed immersions are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage and liftCoborder_ι identify that pullback with j⁻¹(V). This open contains E by j(E) ⊆ V.

source.place: Properties Lemma 01ZY proof, final paragraph: D_+(f) affine and X cap D_+(f) closed in it (closedness argued topologically, X being open)
